race_context: The South Henry School Corporation serves southern Henry County. It was formed in 1963 from schools in Dudley, Franklin and Spiceland townships {wiki_shsc}. Its office is in Lewisville, and it runs two schools, Tri Elementary and Tri Junior-Senior High, with all students from PreK through grade 12 on one campus {sh_home}. The district says about one-third of its students come from outside the district {sh_home}. Tri Junior-Senior High, in Straughn, serves Spiceland, Straughn, Lewisville, New Lisbon and Dunreith and enrolled 458 students in 2024–25, according to federal data cited by Wikipedia {wiki_tri}. This guide did not find a current districtwide enrollment figure.

Superintendent: Sarah Lynch was superintendent through spring 2026 {sh_min_jan26}{sh_min_apr23}. On June 22, 2026 the board voted 4-0 to approve a superintendent contract for Chris Stilwell, and he attended board meetings as superintendent from July 2026 {sh_min_jun22}{sh_min_jul26}. The district's staff directory lists Stilwell as superintendent {sh_staff}.

The board has seven members: President Beth Carr, Vice President Jonathan Willmore, Secretary Lisa Thompson, Randy Paul, Casey Carmichael, Debbie Hicks and Misty Jones {sh_board}{sh_min_jan26}. County election records show the seats are one at large, two for Dudley Township, two for Franklin Township and two for Spiceland Township (one of them a holdover seat) {hc_2022_results}{hc_2024_results}. Hayworth-Jones, Thompson, Carr and Carmichael won the Franklin and Spiceland seats in 2024 and are not on this ballot {hc_2024_results}.

At-large seat: Randy Paul won it in 2022, defeating Jeremiah Cummings 653 votes to 579 {hc_2022_results}. Paul is not on the 2026 candidate list, so the seat is open. The candidates are Cummings (listed as Republican) and Jason Marshall (no party) {hc_2026_list}{in_list}.

Dudley Township seats: in 2022 the Dudley Township race was 'Vote For 2,' and Debra Hicks (1,116 votes) and Jonathan Willmore (716) were the only two candidates {hc_2022_results}{hc_2022_candidates}. Both of those terms end this year. The 2026 county list names two Dudley candidates, Arther W. Claar and incumbent Debra Hicks, and Willmore is not on it {hc_2026_list}. The state list labels the race 'Dudley 2' with 'vote for 1' {in_list}. The 2022 setup suggests both Dudley seats are on the ballot, in which case both candidates would be elected. This guide did not find a 2026 sample ballot to confirm the number of seats.

Budget and property taxes (2025–2026): at the Sept. 9, 2025 meeting, Director of Finance and Business Amy Milner said that because of the coming tax caps and uncertainty over assessed values and state funding, the district had been 'reserving our cash to get us through the ’27 and ’28 budgets' {ct_sep25}. The board approved three resolutions moving money from the Education Fund to the Operations and Rainy Day funds and from the Rainy Day Fund to Operations {ct_sep25}. The district's 2027 budget notice lists a $11,314,743 total budget, with $6,268,557 for Education, $3,456,035 for Operations and $1,540,151 for Debt Service, plus a property tax cap credit estimate of $101,900. The notice set a public hearing for Sept. 22, 2026 and adoption for Oct. 13, 2026 {sh_budget27}.

Facilities (2025–2026): a cafeteria remodel was finished for the start of the 2025–26 school year, and the board used 2025 general obligation bond money for a wheelchair bus, a truck and elementary office HVAC work {ct_sep25}. A Feb. 26, 2026 work session also listed a bus barn, cafeteria HVAC and high school gym air conditioning under the 2025 bond, and a 2026 HELP loan for an activity bus and a 72-passenger bus {sh_min_feb26}. On April 23, 2026 the board approved buying classroom furniture with 2025 bond money {sh_min_apr23}.

Out-of-district students (2026): on March 10, 2026 the board set Feb. 1, 2027 as the date for accepting out-of-district transfer students for 2026–27 {sh_min_mar10}. On June 9, 2026 it approved the number of transfer students each building and grade will take for 2026–27 {sh_min_jun9}.

Policies (2026): on June 9, 2026 the board approved a large set of policy updates on second reading, including policies on personal communication devices and mandatory curriculum {sh_min_jun9}. At the same meeting, a representative of Grace Baptist Church in New Castle presented a proposed policy to allow release time for Bible instruction. The minutes record no board action on it {sh_min_jun9}.
School safety (2026): in June 2026 the board approved contracts for school resource officers Brent Grider and Ric McCorkle and an agreement with the Middletown Police Department {sh_min_jun9}.

Academics: in September 2025 the high school principal said ILEARN Checkpoint would replace NWEA for benchmark testing, and that the district would partner with Indiana Online so students can finish college credits {ct_sep25}.
Forums: this guide found no candidate forums, questionnaires or news coverage of the 2026 South Henry races.
